questions.question: Could we accept 1,000 cardigans by May 30?
questions.expected_answer: Under the current capacity heuristic, accepting 1,000 cardigans by May 30, 2026 is feasible in-house (FEASIBLE_IN_HOUSE). The request was evaluated under the TOPS category. The model counts 52 working days and identifies PACKING as the bottleneck stage, with a median throughput of 672 pieces per working day. This gives an estimated factory window capacity of 34,944 pieces. Existing IN_PROGRESS orders account for 32,850 pieces, leaving an estimated spare factory capacity of 2,094 pieces. Because the requested 1,000 pieces fit within that spare capacity, the order is classified as FEASIBLE_IN_HOUSE. Eligible ACTIVE workshops provide an additional estimated overflow capacity of 52,844.95 pieces, but the in-house verdict does not rely on workshop capacity. This is a planning estimate, not a delivery guarantee. It counts the full piece quantity of every IN_PROGRESS order because remaining quantities are unknown, uses the bottleneck median from the last 30 working days, does not model sequential four-stage pipeline latency, assumes at most one new batch per workshop, and excludes SUSPENDED workshops.

questions.question: Can we take 300 accessories by April 4?
questions.expected_answer: Under the current capacity heuristic, the request for 300 accessories by April 4, 2026 is feasible only with workshops (FEASIBLE_WITH_WORKSHOPS). The request was evaluated under the ACCESSORIES category. The model counts 4 working days and identifies PACKING as the bottleneck stage, with a median throughput of 672 pieces per working day. This gives an estimated factory window capacity of 2,688 pieces. Existing IN_PROGRESS orders account for 32,850 pieces, so the estimated spare factory capacity is clipped to 0. Eligible ACTIVE workshops provide an estimated 418.5 pieces of overflow capacity. Because the requested 300 pieces fit within that estimated workshop capacity, the tool verdict is FEASIBLE_WITH_WORKSHOPS. This is a planning estimate, not a delivery guarantee. It counts the full piece quantity of every IN_PROGRESS order because remaining quantities are unknown, uses the bottleneck median from the last 30 working days, does not model sequential four-stage pipeline latency, assumes at most one new batch per workshop, and excludes SUSPENDED workshops.

按照当前产能模型，无法在 2026 年 4 月 2 日前完成新增 5,000 件围巾订单（NOT_FEASIBLE）。

该订单按 ACCESSORIES（配饰）类别评估。模型计入 2 个工作日，瓶颈为包装环节，其过去 30 个工作日的中位产能是每天 672 件，对应窗口产能 1,344 件。当前在制订单共有 32,850 件，因此工厂剩余产能被裁为 0 件；符合条件的 ACTIVE 外协厂只能再提供约 34.3 件产能，远低于新增的 5,000 件需求。

这是产能规划估算，并非交付保证。模型的限制包括：

由于没有各订单当前阶段的剩余件数，模型将所有在制订单的完整件数计入竞争需求。
工厂产能采用过去 30 个工作日的瓶颈环节中位数，未模拟四个生产环节依次流转所需的时间。
每家外协厂在该窗口内最多按一个新批次计算，并排除暂停合作的外协厂。
结果仅是产能算术检查，不代表实际交付承诺。

questions.question: Can we take 800 hoodies by August 25?
questions.expected_answer:
Yes. Under the current capacity heuristic, 800 hoodies by August 25, 2026 are feasible in-house (FEASIBLE_IN_HOUSE).

The model counts 126 working days and identifies Packing as the bottleneck, with median throughput of 672 pieces per working day. Estimated factory window capacity is 84,672 pieces. After accounting for 32,850 pieces in existing in-progress orders, estimated spare factory capacity is 51,822 pieces, which covers the requested 800 pieces. Active workshops add an estimated 137,034.75 pieces of potential overflow, but they are not required by the verdict.

This is a planning estimate, not a delivery guarantee. It counts every in-progress order’s full quantity because remaining quantities are unknown, uses the bottleneck median from the last 30 working days, and does not model four-stage pipeline latency. Workshop estimates assume one new batch per workshop and exclude suspended workshops.

questions.question: Explain the bottleneck and capacity assumptions in your feasibility result.
questions.expected_answer:
The feasibility result used these assumptions:

Factory bottleneck

• PACKING was the bottleneck because it had the lowest 30-working-day median throughput: 672 pieces per working day.
• The window from April 1 through May 15 contains 39 working days, counting Monday–Saturday and excluding Sundays.
• The model therefore set factory window capacity at 26,208 pieces.
• It treated all 32,850 pieces on IN_PROGRESS orders as competing workload. Because that exceeds the modeled window capacity, spare in-house capacity was clipped to 0.

This is conservative because the dataset does not show how many pieces remain unfinished on each active order; it assumes each order’s entire quantity is still outstanding.

Workshop capacity

Only ACTIVE workshops that make ACCESSORIES were included: W2, W4, and W6. For each workshop:

• Available production days = working days minus pickup lead time and existing queue.
• Output = daily capacity × available days × (1 − defect rate).
• Any maximum batch limit would cap that output.
• The model assumes no more than one new batch per workshop during the window.

Their combined estimated overflow capacity was 12,831.05 pieces. Since the factory had 0 modeled spare capacity but workshop capacity could cover the requested 2,000 scarves, the verdict was FEASIBLE_WITH_WORKSHOPS.

The estimate does not model the timing needed to move work sequentially through knitting, assembly, washing, and packing, so it is a capacity check—not a delivery guarantee.

That 3.0-day figure is calculated as:

max(sum of pieces ÷ 30-day median output for each remaining stage, number of remaining stages)

Because Packing is its only remaining stage, the estimate uses the packing pace for its 2,000 pieces, with a minimum of one day. It is therefore 1st priority: overdue but close to completion.

questions.question: Why is this order considered risky?
questions.expected_answer:
ORD-120 is risky because it is already overdue, not because it is stalled.

Its due date was 2026-03-17. Compared with the factory date of 2026-04-01, the calculation due date − factory today gives −15 calendar days, meaning it is 15 days past due with 0 working days remaining.

It is still in ASSEMBLY, with ASSEMBLY, WASHING, and PACKING left. Its last activity was 2026-03-30, only two working days ago, so it is not flagged as stalled.
